**Visual Analysis:**
- Affected part: corn stalk (cross-section/broken stalk)
- Key features: straw/tan colored rotted stalk tissue, stalk lodging/breakage, and notably **small black dots (pycnidia)** clearly visible scattered on the stalk rind surface
- The interior appears degraded/collapsed

**Reasoning:**
The small black pycnidia (fungal fruiting bodies) scattered on the tan stalk surface are the key diagnostic feature. This is characteristic of **Diplodia stalk rot** (*Stenocarpella maydis*), which produces small black pycnidia on the stalk rind, causing stalk decay and lodging. The reference images confirm: similar straw-colored collapsed stalks with dark spots at the nodes/internodes. The overall appearance — dry tan stalk, visible pycnidia, stalk breakage — aligns strongly with Diplodia stalk rot rather than Anthracnose (which shows more black discoloration of the stalk rind) or Charcoal rot (which shows gray-black internal discoloration with microsclerotia).
